quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Why is it good to keep space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles better.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. If something dangerous happens, you will have more time to react and more room to move safely.

questions.question: If bright sun makes it hard to see a motorcycle's turn signals, the rider should:

options.text: Keep using the mechanical turn signals.
Honk the horn to tell drivers about turns.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sun makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Check your mirrors only. Look over your shoulder only if something seems wrong.
Either check mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, make sure no other vehicles are in your path. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block the view.

questions.explanation: Do not rely only on mirrors to see what is around you. Motorcycles have blind spots just like any other vehicle.

questions.question: What helps others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Move back and forth in your lane.
Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlight to help other drivers see your motorcycle. Always check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT greatly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content (BAC) is mainly affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: What should you do about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They do not exist if the motorcycle has a mirror.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make this a regular habit.

questions.question: When riding near a truck:

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
Do not worry about the truck's mirrors and focus on your riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Stay out of blind spots, especially around large trucks. Remember: if you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When being passed, moving far from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is a good idea because you are farther away.
Is not a good idea because it may make the other driver move back too early.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not a good idea because it may make the other driver move back too early.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far part of your lane when being passed. This may tell the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. If you use only the rear brake, you may not learn how to use the front brake properly when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Experienced riders use the acronym "SIPDE" to stay aware of road conditions. What does the "D" stand for?
questions.explanation: SIPDE is a five-step process for safe riding. The letters stand for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Accidentally drift into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accidentally drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a potential problem?

options.text: A change in road surface coming up
Conditions that do not change as you approach

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that do not change as you approach
questions.explanation: Anticipate problems on the road and make a plan to stay safe. Conditions that stay the same are not a concern.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle takes:

options.text: Less time to stop and speed up.
The same time to stop and speed up.
More time to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows down acceleration and deceleration. Your motorcycle responds more slowly with a passenger than when you ride alone.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Cover the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.explanation: Approaching an intersection: choose a visible lane position, cover the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time, and reduce speed. Do not change speed or position suddenly, as this confuses other drivers.

questions.question: What can remove alcohol from a person's body?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold air cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: Most motorcycle and automobile accidents occur:
questions.explanation: Most collisions between motorcycles and cars happen at intersections. Usually the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to start moving.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns drivers that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: Before riding, check your motorcycle's clutch. A working clutch should feel:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your clutch and throttle. The throttle should snap back when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat, your steering will suddenly feel:
questions.explanation: Heavy steering is a sign your front tire may be flat. Stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet when riding a moving motorcycle?
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when on a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.
